hints.alg.inequalities.solve: Solve it like an equation: undo the number, then divide. Keep the same sign. Tap the sign first, then type the number.
hints.alg.inequalities.flip: When you divide both sides by a negative number, flip the sign: < becomes >, ≤ becomes ≥.
hints.alg.inequalities: Solve like an equation. If you divide by a negative number, flip the sign. Check with a number.

misconceptionMessages.alg.ineq-no-flip: You divided by a negative number, so the sign has to flip: −3x < 12 becomes x > −4.
misconceptionMessages.alg.ineq-flipped-anyway: Only flip when you multiply or divide by a NEGATIVE number. A negative answer doesn't flip anything.
misconceptionMessages.alg.ineq-or-equal: Keep the "or equal to" part: if the problem has ≤ or ≥, the answer does too (flipped or not).
misconceptionMessages.alg.ineq-wrong-inverse: Undo the number the opposite way: 2x − 5 ≥ 7 means ADD 5 to both sides, so 2x ≥ 12.

sections.title: Solve like an equation
explain: An inequality has many answers: x > 6 means any number bigger than 6.
Undo the steps like an equation. Check with a number that should work.
sections.key: Solve an inequality like an equation: do the same thing to both sides. Adding, subtracting, or dividing by a positive number keeps the sign.

worked.note: check with a number bigger than 6

sections.title: Flip the sign
sections.objective: Flip the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.
explain: Multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number reverses the order of numbers, so the sign flips.
Adding and subtracting never flip it.

visual.caption: 2 < 5. Multiply both by −1 and watch the order.

sections.key: Dividing (or multiplying) both sides by a negative number flips the sign: < becomes >, ≤ becomes ≥.

worked.note: divide by −3 and flip the sign
check: 0 is bigger than −4, and it works

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.key: Solve like an equation. Divide by a negative number? Flip the sign. Then check with a number.
